heading: Gaps
reported_value: O2 tolerated up to 1% for e.g. Fischer-Tropsch; no efficient continuous method to reach <1% found
evidence_excerpt_or_description: For many applications of the CO gas (e.g. Fischer-Tropsch fuel synthesis) oxygen concentration is tolerated only in small quantities up to maximum 1% ... So far, an efficient way to remove large amounts of oxygen (reaching below 1% concentration) in a continuous way has not been found

heading: Operating conditions

notes: scaling of conversion and efficiency with power 'yet to be demonstrated'

heading: Performance indicators
reported_value: 70 kW system; 1.0 A/cm2; 800 C short-stack IV; CO2 utilisation 86% (max, to avoid carbon); CO 17.5 m3/h; stack 69.6 kW; wall-plug 89.0%; EPC 3.89 kWh/Nm3; rectifier/inverter 0.95 assumed
evidence_excerpt_or_description: A current density of 1.0 A/cm2 was taken and the CO2-utilisation, which equals the CO2-conversion, was set at a maximum value of 86% to prevent any carbon formation, which might occur at higher conversion ratios. This results in an CO outflow of 17.5 m3/h with an electrical input to the stack of 69.6 kW. The wall plug efficiency amounts to 89.0% with an electric power consumption (EPC) of 3.89 kWh/Nm3CO
basis_and_boundary: process-engineering calculation from measured short-stack IV (Fig. 4b), flow scheme adapted from ref. 111
notes: not a measured system; reported 3.89 likely a typo for 3.98 (C001)
